Name: Patch Information Version B
Description: The Patch Information Version B (PATCHB) TRE provides information describing a portion of an image, a patch, to support exploitation. This TRE contains support data pertaining to a single image patch, and one PATCH extension is created for each image patch.

PAT_NO.Name: Patch Number
PAT_NO.Description: This field contains the patch number. Patches are numbered consecutively, starting with 0001, for each image within a file.

LAST_PAT_FLAG.Name: Last Patch of Search Scene
LAST_PAT_FLAG.Description: This field is a flag to indicate that this patch is the last in a search scene. When all patches of a scene are not contained within a single file, PATCH_TOT in ACFTB cannot indicate the total number of patches in the scene. This flag then makes it clear that the scene ends with this patch. 0 = Not End, 1 = End.

LNSTRT.Name: Line Start
LNSTRT.Description: This field contains the absolute starting line number of this patch within an overall image (scene). This field provides similar information to ILOC in the image subheader, but in a form more suitable for some operations. This field identifies specifically where this patch fits relative to the other N patches comprising an overall scene, whereas relative values in ILOC are referenced to the object to which this patch is attached.

LNSTOP.Name: Line Stop
LNSTOP.Description: This field contains the absolute ending line number of this patch within an overall image (scene). This field provides similar information to ILOC in the image subheader, but in a form more suitable for some operations. This field identifies specifically where this patch fits relative to the other N patches comprising an overall scene, whereas relative values in ILOC are referenced to the object to which this patch is attached.

AZL.Name: Number of Azimuth Lines in Current Patch
AZL.Description: This field contains the number of azimuth lines in the current patch.

NVL.Name: Number of Valid Azimuth Line
NVL.Description: This field contains the number of valid azimuth lines.

FVL.Name: First Valid Line
FVL.Description: This field contains the first valid line. In some Spot modes, the Spot scene does not always completely fill the frame. Therefore, these variables together describe the location of the valid imagery within the azimuth lines transferred. These variables have no such meaning in the Search modes.

NPIXEL.Name: Number of Pixels
NPIXEL.Description: This field contains the number of image pixels per line. For both Spot and Search, the value range for this field is 00001 to 99999.

FVPIX.Name: First Valid Pixel Index
FVPIX.Description: This field contains the location of the first pixel on a line. This variable, with the number of pixels per line, will define the location of valid data in the image. For both Spot and Search, the valid range for this field is 00001 to 99999.

FRAME.Name: Spot Frame Number
FRAME.Description: This field contains the spot frame number. In Continuous Spot Mode, each image about the same Map Center (a single scene) is called a Frame. The Frame Number starts at 001 and is incremented by 1 for each frame of the scene. This field contains spaces for Search and Single Spot modes.

UTC.Name: Coordinated Universal Time
UTC.Description: The time in seconds (accurate to 0.01 seconds) of the start of the current patch or, in the case of Spot, the current scene or frame. UTC uses a 24-hour clock where a value of 00000.00 corresponds to midnight.

SHEAD.Name: Scene Heading
SHEAD.Description: The Scene Heading is a variable that references the scene to True North. In Search Scenes, it is the angle from True North clockwise to the Scene Center Line. In Spotlight Scenes, it is the angle from True North clockwise to the Azimuth Vector (projection of the line of sight from the sensor onto a horizontal plane).

GRAVITY.Name: Local Gravity
GRAVITY.Description: This field defines the local gravity in feet/second^2.

INS_V_NC.Name: Ins Platform Velocity, North
INS_V_NC.Description: This field contains the Ins Platform Velocity, North. The Inertial Navigator Platform velocity is given in a North, East, Down earth-fixed coordinate system. The measurements are given in units of feet/second. These parameters are only valid at the time specified by UTC.

INS_V_EC.Name: Ins Platform Velocity, East
INS_V_EC.Description: This field contains the Ins Platform Velocity, East. The Inertial Navigator Platform velocity is given in a North, East, Down earth-fixed coordinate system. The measurements are given in units of feet/second. These parameters are only valid at the time specified by UTC.

INS_V_DC.Name: Ins Platform Velocity, Down
INS_V_DC.Description: This field contains the Ins Platform Velocity, Down. The Inertial Navigator Platform velocity is given in a North, East, Down earth-fixed coordinate system. The measurements are given in units of feet/second. These parameters are only valid at the time specified by UTC.

OFFLAT.Name: Geodetic Latitude Offset
OFFLAT.Description: The Geodetic Latitude Offset is the accumulated latitude correction currently being used to correct the Inertial Navigation System (INS) aircraft position outputs. The offset is given in seconds of a degree; North and East are positive.

OFFLON.Name: Geodetic Longitude Offset
OFFLON.Description: The Geodetic Longitude Offset is the accumulated longitude correction currently being used to correct the Inertial Navigation System (INS) aircraft position outputs. The offset is given in seconds of a degree; North and East are positive.

TRACK.Name: Track Heading
TRACK.Description: The track heading is measured in degrees relative to true North. The measurement is clockwise about the vertical from North to the projection of the aircraft roll axis into th elevel plane, and is valid at the time specified by UTC.

GSWEEP.Name: Ground Sweep Angle
GSWEEP.Description: The ground sweep angle is determined by the required azimuth resolution and is the angle over which phase history is collected. The measurements are given in degrees.

SHEAR.Name: Patch Shear Factor
SHEAR.Description: This field contains the patch shear factor. Targets are imaged in the slant plane determined by the Processing Central Reference Point and the SAR velocity vector at mid-array. The conversion from target spacing in the ground plane to target spacing in the slant plane for each patch allows the optimal matching of terrain features in one patch to those in the next.

BATCH_NO.Name: Batch Number
BATCH_NO.Description: This field contains the consecutive number for coherent files collected during a mission.
